approaches_tried.approach: git stash to isolate task 688's uncommitted work before checking baseline on a clean tree
approaches_tried.reason: stashed the entire shared working tree (other concurrently-dispatched tasks' uncommitted files too); stash pop then conflicted with a sibling's fresh edit and aborted. Recovered this task's 3 owned files by extracting them from the stash via `git show stash@{0}:<path> > <path>`. CORRECTION (added post-hoc by teammate review): that extraction was NOT a complete recovery -- it missed that the failed pop had also silently reverted specs/events.jsonl (an unowned, append-only, no-conflict file), dropping 32 telemetry rows, because an append-only file gives no conflict signal and nothing in this task's own file scope pointed at it. A teammate caught the row-count regression and merged the lost rows back in from the still-present stash@{0} before postflight committed the file. See the phase-1 handoff's Addendum for the full account. Lesson: never run a bare `git stash`/`git stash pop` on a shared tree with concurrent siblings -- selective extraction of only your own declared files is not sufficient recovery, since an unowned append-only file can be silently reverted with no visible sign.
